Q79358625.label: Manuel Marrero Cruz
Q79358625.desc: Prime Minister of the Republic of Cuba
Q79358625.img: Manuel Marrero Cruz before the funeral of Shinzo Abe.jpg
Q79358625.summary: Manuel Marrero Cruz is a Cuban politician who has served as prime minister of Cuba since 2019. He was the first prime minister appointed after the position was abolished in 1976 and reestablished in a constitutional referendum. A member of the Communist Party of Cuba, he served as minister of tourism from 2004 until his appointment as prime minister. During his tenure as minister for tourism, Cuba underwent a massive boost in tourism. Marrero is an architect and worked in Gaviota, the tourism arm of the Cuban military, where he also held the rank of colonel.

Positions held: member of the National Assembly of People's Power

Q7842465.label: 1995 Trinidad and Tobago general election
Q7842465.desc: general election in Trinidad and Tobago
Q7842465.summary: Early general elections were held in Trinidad and Tobago on 6 November 1995, after the ruling People's National Movement had seen its majority reduced to a single seat due to a defection and a lost by-election. The results saw the PNM and the United National Congress both win 17 seats.

Q951969.label: Manuel Esquivel
Q951969.summary: Sir Manuel Amadeo Esquivel was a Belizean politician. As leader of the United Democratic Party, he served as the second prime minister of Belize from 1984 to 1989, and then again from 1993 to 1998. His party's victory in 1984 was the first time an opposition party had won a general election in Belize.

Q5174945.label: 1946 Costa Rican parliamentary election
Q5174945.summary: Mid-term parliamentary elections were held in Costa Rica on 10 February 1946. The result was a victory for the National Republican Party, which received 51% of the vote. Voter turnout was 64%. They were the last mid-term elections in the country's history.

Q104866465.label: 1967 Anguillian general election
Q104866465.summary: General elections were planned to be held in Anguilla on 25 October 1967 following the Anguillian Revolution in May. However, only five candidates stood for the five seats, with all elected unopposed.

Q156833.label: Ramiz Alia
Q156833.desc: former First Secretary of the Party of Labour of Albania, 1st President of the Republic of Albania (1925-2011)
Q156833.summary: Ramiz Alia was an Albanian politician serving as the second and last leader of the People's Socialist Republic of Albania from 1985 to 1991, serving as First Secretary of the Party of Labour of Albania. He was also the country's head of state from 1982 to 1992. He had been seen as a successor by Enver Hoxha and took power after Hoxha died.

Q29584545.label: 2017 Albanian presidential election
Q29584545.summary: Indirect presidential elections were held in Albania on 19, 20, 27 and 28 April 2015, the eighth such elections since the collapse of the communist regime in 1991. In the first through third round, no candidates were proposed and no vote took place in the Parliament of Albania.

Q3722401.label: 2000 Serbian parliamentary election
Q3722401.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Serbia on 23 December 2000, to elect members of the National Assembly. They were the first free and fair parliamentary elections since the re-introduction of a multi-party system in 1990 and the overthrow of Slobodan Milošević.

Q20182177.label: 2019 Lithuanian presidential election
Q20182177.desc: 7th election of the 1990 Republic of Lithuania
Q20182177.summary: Presidential elections were held in Lithuania on 12 May 2019, with a second round held on 26 May 2019. Due to a constitutional limit of two terms in office, incumbent president Dalia Grybauskaitė was unable to run, having won the 2009 and 2014 elections.

Q328353.label: 2006 Ukrainian parliamentary election
Q328353.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Ukraine on 26 March 2006. Election campaigning officially began on 7 July 2005. Between November 26 and 31 December 2005, party lists of candidates were formed.

Q84081313.label: 2024 Belarusian parliamentary election
Q84081313.img: Logo for the 2024 Belarusian parliamentary and local elections.png
Q84081313.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Belarus on 25 February 2024. The country elected 110 deputies to the lower house of parliament and 12,514 representatives of local councils.

Q2917025.label: 1984 Israeli legislative election
Q2917025.summary: Legislative elections were held in Israel on 23 July 1984 to elect the eleventh Knesset. Voter turnout was 78.8%. The results saw the Alignment return to being the largest party in the Knesset, a status it had lost in 1977.

Q358561.label: Reinhold Niebuhr
Q358561.summary: Karl Paul Reinhold Niebuhr was an American Mainline Protestant theologian in the Reformed tradition, ethicist, commentator on politics and public affairs, and professor at Union Theological Seminary for more than 30 years. Niebuhr was one of America's leading public intellectuals for several decades of the 20th century and received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 1964. A public theologian, he wrote and spoke frequently about the intersection of religion, politics, and public policy, with his most influential books including Moral Man and Immoral Society and The Nature and Destiny of Man.

Member of: American Academy of Arts and Letters
